To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the release of Ca2 +from internal Ca2+stores in CH12.LX cells activates a Ca2+-selective channel that is electrogenic and that the channel is activated by a rise in intracellular free Ca2+.

(1) Ca2+ release from the internal store is followed by an electrogenic Ca‐permeable pathway, (2) the electrogenic pathway is inhibited by Ni2+ and is not affected by Na+ substitution, (3) this pathway can be inhibited by the addition of charybdotoxim, and (4) the electrogenic Ca2+-permeable pathway is regulated by the internal Ca2+ store.
the electrogenic plasma membrane pathway for Ca2+ uptake is regulated in a complex manner by the degree of Ca2+ filling of intracellular stores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium in the regulation of cellular processes.
the regulation of Ca(2+)-dependent processes.
the role of intracelluar calcium stores in the regulation and control of the electrogenic Ca2+-permeable pathway in B-lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ca2+ ‐activated K+ channels are involved in the regulation of intracellular Ca stores.
the Ca‐permeable pathway in the B‐lymphoid cell line is regulated by the filling state of an internal Ca store.
the electrogenic Ca2+-permeable pathway in the B-lymphocytic cells is regulated by the internal store of Ca2+ and the degree of filling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that the electrogenic Ca2+-uptake pathway in B-lymphocytic cells is regulated by the level of filling of an intracellular Ca2+-store.
the Ca2+ uptake system of the B‐lymphocyte cell line CH12 is electrogenic, and regulated by intracellular Ca2+, and that this regulation is mediated by a store‐gated pathway.
the intracellular Ca2+-store regulates the electrogenic plasma membrane calcium uptake in the B‐lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a pathway for Ca2+ uptake that is electrogenic.
the intracellular Ca2+-store regulates the electrogenic Ca2+-permeable pathway.
there is a Ca2+ ‐activated K+ channel that is regulated by the filling state of an internal Ca‐store.
